courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon successful completion of this course, students should be able to:

1. To become acquainted with the key filmmakers, works, themes, and issues in Southeast Asian cinema
2. To explain how film and media representations visualize and problematize the distinct social, economic, political, and historical conditions of diverse Southeast Asian cultures
3. To apply a comparative, transnational lens to examine film and media representations that illustrate how these diverse Southeast Asian cultures have become articulated in Hong Kong
courses.course_syllabus:
* *Week 1: Visualizing Southeast Asia**

* How do scholars, filmmakers, and artists imagine Southeast Asia?

* *Week 2: Inter-Orientalism**

* How have commercial movies, television shows, and tourism campaigns visualized the landscapes and populations of Southeast Asia with an orientalist gaze?

* *Week 3: Remediating Genres**

* How does Southeast Asian cinema reinvent the generic conventions of Western, spy, martial arts, and science fiction films?

* *Week 4: Crime Noir and Slum Voyeurism**

* How do film noir, crime thrillers, and poverty porn characterize the settings of Southeast Asian megalopolises with destitution, squalor, and violence?

* *Week 5: Racial Border-Crossings**

* How does Southeast Asian cinema ruminate on issues of race and multiculturalism?

* *Week 6: Migrant Labor Mobilities**

* How do melodramas and documentaries spotlight the victimization of migrant workers?

* *Week 7: Ghosts, Monsters, and Spiritualities**

* How do ghost, monster, and horror movies explore the link between spirituality and development?

* *Week 8: Historical Memory**

* How do period epics and experimental films construct and reexamine historical representations?

* *Week 9: Documentary Trauma**

* How do reflexive documentaries explore the trauma of political violence in Southeast Asia?

* *Week 10: Stardom**

* How have popular movie stars in Southeast Asia shaped social identity?

* *Week 11: Theaters and Spaces**

* How do cinema and historiography represent the spaces of film distribution and exhibition?

* *Week 12: Seriality and Regionalism**

* How do omnibus films, serial dramas, and digital artworks imagine a pan-regional community?

* *Week 13: Field trip to sites in Hong Kong with historical or cultural significance to Southeast Asia**

* Possible destinations include the Dr. Sun Yat-sen Museum, Kowloon City, and Filipinas Heritage Trail.

* *Week 14: Presentation and submission of paper**

* As a synthesis of the class materials and discussions for the entire semester, the final paper will examine the film and media culture of Southeast Asia in Hong Kong. Students can opt to work on the final paper individually, in pairs, or in groups. Possible topics include how Vietnamese boat people, Filipino and Indonesian domestic workers, Burmese Buddhist monks, or Kowloon City’s Thai community are visualized in Hong Kong’s cinema, news, advertising, and social media.

courses.subject: UGEC
courses.title: Language Disorders
courses.description:
(UGEC3928 is double-coded with LING3208.)
This survey course introduces non-clinical students to fundamental concepts of language disorders in paediatric and adult populations. Characteristics of primary language impairment, aphasia, dysarthria, and hearing impairments, as well as articulation, fluency, and voice and other related disorders affecting language are among the topics to be discussed. Diagnostic techniques and treatment strategies are also introduced.

Discussions will be made on the impacts of language impairment on one’s cognitive development, academic performance, as well as physical, psychological and social well-being across the lifespan (SDG#3 Good Health and Well-Being). Students will be able to gain a better understanding of how people suffering from these disorders are deprived from healthy lives (SDG#3 Good Health and Well-Being), quality education (SDG#4 Quality Education), employment opportunities (SDG#8 Decent Work and Economic Growth), and social equality (SDG#10 Reduced Inequalities). Students will also come to appreciate the benefits brought by the relevant assessment and treatment in promoting personal wellbeing (SDG#3 Good Health and Well-Being), ensuring inclusive and equitable quality education (SDG#4 Quality Education), providing full and productive employment and decent work for all (SDG#8 Decent Work and Economic Growth), as well as reducing inequality in the society (SDG#10 Reduced Inequalities).

courses.learning_outcomes:
At the end of the course, students will be able to

* Describe the fundamentals of language and communication, and basic characteristics of language disorders
* Explain the etiology of different language disorders
* Analyze patient signs and symptoms and attribute them to specific language disorder types, and reflect on how these disorders may create barriers to quality education for children (SDG#4 Quality Education) and decent work for adults (SDG#8 Decent Work and Economic Growth)
* Identify and analyze the problems brought by language disorders with respect to good health and wellbeing (SDG#3 Good Health and Well-Being), quality education (SDG#4 Quality Education), decent work (SDG#8 Decent Work and Economic Growth), and inequality reduction (SDG#10 Reduced Inequalities)
* Investigate how the diagnostic techniques and treatment strategies can serve to solve the problems brought by language disorders, including those from disadvantaged backgrounds (SDG#10 Reduced Inequalities)
* Evaluate the difficulties and challenging in implementing assessment and treatment for language disorders for all peoples (SDG#10 Reduced Inequalities)
* Reflect on the role they can play in promoting wellbeing for all members of the society regardless of their visible and invisible limitations to participate in society (SDG#3 Good Health and Well-Being)
courses.course_syllabus:
* *Foundations of language and communication**

* Systems of communication, classification of disorders

* *Biological foundations of language**

* Anatomy & physiology of the vocal mechanism and the brain

* *Psychometrics, normalcy & variation in language development and functions (SDG#3, #4, #8, #10)**

* Stages of speech, language, and literacy development

* *Speech disorders (SDG#3, #4, #8, #10)**

* Articulation & phonological disorders in children, fluency disorders, voice disorders, and dysarthria
* Characteristics, assessment, and treatment
* Associations between language problems and cognitive development/well-being (SDG#3 Good Health and Well-Being)
* Problems brought by speech disorders on quality education (SDG#4 Quality Education), employment opportunities (SDG#8 Decent Work and Economic Growth) and economic equality (SDG#10 Reduced Inequalities)

* *Language disorders in children (SDG#3, #4, #8, #10)**

* Primary language impairment, literacy problem, and genetic syndromes
* Characteristics, assessment, and treatment
* Associations between language problems and cognitive development (SDG#3 Good Health and Well-Being)
* Problems brought by language disorders on quality education (SDG#4 Quality Education), employment opportunities (SDG#8 Decent Work and Economic Growth) and economic equality (SDG#10 Reduced Inequalities)

* *Neurogenic disorders in adults (SDG#3, #8, #10)**

* Aphasia and cognitive-based communication disorders
* Characteristics, assessment, and treatment
* Associations between language problems and cognitive well-being (SDG#3 Good Health and Well-Being)
* Problems brought by neurogenic disorders on employment opportunities (SDG#8 Decent Work and Economic Growth) and economic equality (SDG#10 Reduced Inequalities)

* *Hearing impairment and language (SDG#3, #4, #8, #10)**

* Deafness, cochlear implant, and aging
* Characteristics, assessment, and treatment
* Associations between language problems and cognitive well-being (SDG#3 Good Health and Well-Being)
* Problems brought by hearing impairment on employment opportunities (SDG#8 Decent Work and Economic Growth) and economic equality (SDG#10 Reduced Inequalities)

* *Disorders in multi-lingual speakers (SDG#3, #4, #8, #10)**

* Characteristics, assessment, and treatment
* Associations between language problems and cognitive well-being (SDG#3 Good Health and Well-Being)
* Problems brought by language disorders on quality education (SDG#4 Quality Education), employment opportunities (SDG#8 Decent Work and Economic Growth) and economic equality (SDG#10 Reduced Inequalities)
